correctness.rationale: Proof Steps 1–3 restrict the unique compact-set minimum disk to symmetry-axis centers, obtain F’=2f’(H-z), screen all interior graph points by monotone H, and minimize the exact three-point maximum. Step 4 establishes strict H growth for catenaries using B’=sinh(t)(3sinh(t)cosh(t)-t)>0. Steps 5–6 prove the unique root, exact quadratic onset, and power-arch boundary. The embedded standalone checker passed 150015 finite catenary checks; the proof does not rely on finite sampling. No unproved global maximization lemma remains.

value.rationale: A motivated continuum 1-center problem for hanging-chain arches is reduced *exactly* to three measured points throughout a nontrivial analytic class, yielding a closed radius and center, uniqueness and a sharp two-to-three support transition. The square-law singularity and the sharp failure for flatter-than-quadratic power arches expose a meaningful geometric boundary; these facts are not mere substitutions into a finite-point algorithm. The exact profile is relevant to enclosing-window design and rigorous finite-sample screening for curved boundaries.
